officialTitle: Osimertinib in Untreated EGFR-Mutated Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: we randomly assigned 556 patients with previously untreated, EGFR mutation-positive (exon 19 deletion or L858R) advanced NSCLC in a 1:1 ratio

clinicalQuestion: Is the third-generation EGFR TKI osimertinib superior to first-generation EGFR TKIs (gefitinib or erlotinib) as first-line therapy for EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC?

pico.population: Previously untreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R
pico.outcomes: Primary: investigator-assessed PFS. Secondary: OS, ORR, DoR, safety

arms.label: Osimertinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive either osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily)

arms.label: Standard EGFR-TKI
arms.dosing: Gefitinib 250 mg once daily or erlotinib 150 mg once daily
arms.doseSourceQuote: a standard EGFR-TKI (gefitinib at a dose of 250 mg once daily or erlotinib at a dose of 150 mg once daily)

publications.title: Osimertinib in Untreated EGFR-Mutated Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

publications.title: Overall Survival with Osimertinib in Untreated,-Mutated Advanced NSCLC.
publications.label: Final overall survival analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median progression-free survival was significantly longer with osimertinib than with standard EGFR-TKIs (18.9 months vs. 10.2 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.37 to 0.57; P<0.001).
The objective response rate was similar in the two groups: 80% with osimertinib and 76% with standard EGFR-TKIs (odds ratio, 1.27; 95% CI, 0.85 to 1.90; P=0.24).
The median duration of response was 17.2 months (95% CI, 13.8 to 22.0) with osimertinib versus 8.5 months (95% CI, 7.3 to 9.8) with standard EGFR-TKIs.

The survival rate at 18 months was 83% (95% CI, 78 to 87) with osimertinib and 71% (95% CI, 65 to 76) with standard EGFR-TKIs (hazard ratio for death, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.88; P=0.007 [nonsignificant in the interim analysis]).

The median overall survival was 38.6 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 34.5 to 41.8) in the osimertinib group and 31.8 months (95% CI, 26.6 to 36.0) in the comparator group (hazard ratio for death, 0.80; 95.05% CI, 0.64 to 1.00; P = 0.046).

safety.description: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher (primary analysis)
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher were less frequent with osimertinib than with standard EGFR-TKIs (34% vs. 45%).

safety.description: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher (final OS analysis)
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher were reported in 42% of the patients in the osimertinib group and in 47% of those in the comparator group.

strengths: Double-blind randomised design with an active TKI comparator
Both PFS and final OS favoured osimertinib
limitations: Comparator arm pooled two first-generation EGFR TKIs

clinicalImplications.text: Established osimertinib as a preferred first-line EGFR TKI for EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R advanced NSCLC, with PFS benefit confirmed by a longer overall survival in the final analysis.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Using the best TKI first beat the sequencing strategy of first-generation TKI followed by osimertinib at T790M progression in this trial.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 29151359 (primary) and PMID 31751012 (final OS). Arm n taken from final OS abstract quote ('79 of 279 ... 26 of 277'); verify against full text.
